Oh that's a common bra construction. Called "leotard back" or "u back". Basically the straps aren't just attached vertically to the band. Instead when they reach the band they start curving towards the bra clasp. So instead of looking like a ham being criss crossed by strings it smooths everything out.
Thanks for explaining. I don't have back fat (or tits for that matter) so I was wondering how this was supposed to work.

This construction is not only for back fat, that's like a side effect because theres a bit more coverage. It mostly helps with weight distribution and helping the bra band keep its elasticity. The material in a bra is usually pretty stretchy and construction is key in finding the balance of it stretching to accommodate it's owner but not stretching enough to lose its support.

Bra straps are usually made of a sturdier material that still stretches but when you pull it there's a definite "stop" moment where you cant pull more. So if the bra strap continues right up to the bra clasp that means the top edge of the band is lined with this sturdier material.
